title: Implement timebound prefetch throttle and tenant fairness watchdog
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (notably Acme Health and NimbusDocs) reported intermittent severe p99 latency regressions for short requests during bursts of long-context generation. The visible symptom is short-request starvation: short, latency-sensitive flows are queued behind long-context batches and experience multi-second tail latency despite available GPU throughput. The problem is reproducible across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes and correlates with aggressive prefetch behavior that floods KV cache prefetch windows and forces eviction thrashing.

Root cause hypothesis: The continuous-batcher prefetch path is attempting to prime KV cache aggressively for long-context requests without a bounded admission leash. When a burst of long-context arrivals occurs, prefetch work consumes admission tokens and inflight window slots for an extended duration, causing short requests to be blocked until prefetch completes or eviction stabilizes. Under mixed tenancy and mixed-hosting deployments this gets amplified by cross-tenant admission skew and leftover prefetch fence state that doesn't time out promptly.

Proposed change: 1) Add a timebound prefetch throttle: each prefetch work unit will acquire a soft lease (admission leash) limited to X ms (configurable, default 120ms). If prefetch work exceeds the lease, it will yield and requeue behind latency-sensitive admissions. 2) Implement a tenant fairness watchdog: lightweight per-host watcher computing an admission_fairness_score and proactively demoting long-context prefetches when short_request_p50/p95 delta exceeds threshold. 3) Introduce an adaptive dequeue window that temporarily increases preemptive dequeue frequency when short-request queue depth crosses a threshold. 4) Add metrics and telemetry (see monitoring_and_alerts) and a canary rollout plan with gradual percentage increases and automatic rollback on regressions.

Why this is different from prior fixes: earlier patches focused on admission-window sizing and eviction hysteresis; this change targets the prefetch execution model itself and adds a timebound rhythm plus a fairness-domain watchdog that can operate across Hosted/Dedicated/Private without requiring host-level config changes. It is designed to mitigate both transient microbursts and sustained long-context waves gracefully.

Engineering tradeoffs: - Risk: Yielding prefetch early may slightly increase latency for the originating long-context request (extra prefetch roundtrips) but prevents catastrophic starvation for short flows. - Complexity: Watchdog introduces cross-request signal aggregation; we will keep it probabilistic and host-local to avoid global coordination. - Config surface: Provide sane defaults and server flags for enterprise/private customers to tune.

Acceptance criteria:
- Short-request p99 (short_request_p99) must not regress beyond baseline by more than 10% during representative mixed workloads (synthetic mixed-length load + production traffic replay).
- Long-context latency increase (long_context_p50) should be <= 15% in worst-case canary traffic.
- KV eviction_rate must decrease by >= 25% from current peak in replay tests.
- No increase in error rate or OOMs during canary.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for lease acquisition/release, watchdog scoring, and adaptive dequeue triggers.
- Integration test harness: mixed-length generator replaying a 24-hour production trace and injecting microbursts.
- Private cluster smoke in lab with 3 tenants; Dedicated node soak for 48h.
- Hosted canary: rollout 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health gates at each step.

Rollout plan: See rollout_plan.
acceptance_criteria: 1) short_request_p99 <= baseline * 1.10 under mixed-replay. 2) long_context_p50 <= baseline * 1.15. 3) kv_eviction_rate reduced by >=25% on replay. 4) no new errors or instability in 48h soak during canary.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag and default off. 2) Lab validation and integration tests green. 3) Canary: enable feature flag for 1% Hosted traffic for 4 hours; check metrics. 4) If stable, expand to 10% for 12h; validate. 5) Expand to 50% for 24h; validate with Dedicated and one Private pilot. 6) Full rollout. 7) If at any gate short_request_p99 increases >10% or kv_eviction_rate increases, auto-rollback and alert oncall.
monitoring_and_alerts:
Add dashboards and alerts: 1) short_request_p50/p95/p99 by tenant and by host; 2) long_context_p50/p95; 3) admission_fairness_score (new metric) by host; 4) kv_eviction_rate and kv_prefetch_time; 5) prefetch_lease_yields per host; 6) queue_depth_short_requests. Alerts: P1 if short_request_p99 > baseline * 1.15 for >5m; P0 if p99 spike with error increase.
Links to dashboards and example queries will be added to the PR description.
